### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 85b4ac634e3f3997bee7cf038090d24d029bc82c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f645a16a4b9b6f081d6faba8eccd2af16cfc9414` — the merge of head `70c36c11516537a824ada5dadc0bf8c6455f43d3` into base `85b4ac634e3f3997bee7cf038090d24d029bc82c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f645a16a4b9b6f081d6faba8eccd2af16cfc9414 && git checkout f645a16a4b9b6f081d6faba8eccd2af16cfc9414
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 85b4ac634e3f3997bee7cf038090d24d029bc82c 70c36c11516537a824ada5dadc0bf8c6455f43d3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 85b4ac634e3f3997bee7cf038090d24d029bc82c && git merge --no-ff 70c36c11516537a824ada5dadc0bf8c6455f43d3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 85b4ac634e3f3997bee7cf038090d24d029bc82c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `70c36c11516537a824ada5dadc0bf8c6455f43d3`
Local-runs: none

Isolated at-tier review of PR #22931 (card #22902), rendered 2026-10-12T03:56Z. Inputs: the card body and its four comments (triage `6114801402`, claim `6116309776`, `os-dev-report` `6117331386`, ACCEPT `6117358389`), the PR body, its file list, the net diff against `main` at the head above, and the head's check-runs. Base facts were read from `origin/main` (`git show`), nothing was built, run or re-run. The diff is 4 paths, +334 / −2, equal to the PR's file list and to the claim's file surface; the head repo is the base repo (not a fork); no governed surface is touched.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, named and judged:

1. **`defineStack` (strict, the default) now refuses two or more entries of one stack's `functions` ARRAY that author one `name`** — `collectDuplicateFunctionNameErrors`, pushed from `validateCrossReferences`. **Right.** The array member of `functions` on `main` (`stack.zod.ts` `:705`–`:731`) is `z.array(z.object({ name: z.string(), handler, packageId?, effect? }))` with no uniqueness refinement, so `name` is always a string and the `Map` grouping is sound. The refusal is the one-stack sibling of two existing refusals read on `main`: `collectDuplicateActionKeyErrors` (same aggregate, same `joinDeclarationOrigins` spelling `a, b and c`, same `twice` / `N times` wording) and `composeFunctions`' cross-stack `claim()` (`STACK_COMPOSE_FUNCTION_CONFLICT`, `:2591`). This is the card's direction and triage's.
2. **Placement before the object-count early return** (an object-less stack is refused too). **Right.** On `main` `validateCrossReferences` pushes the action-key, global-update and job-pull collectors before `if (objectNames.size === 0) return errors;`; the new push sits in that block for the same reason the comment gives.
3. **Envelope reuse — `StackCrossReferenceError`, `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID`, `status: 422`, one `issues` entry per finding; no new error code.** **Right.** The single raise site (`defineStack`, `:4054`ff on `main`) wraps every collector's lines in that envelope; the family docblock already says the aggregate is wider than "undefined object", and the diff adds `duplicate-function-name` to that sentence. No `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` edit is owed.
4. **The map form is unvisited** (`if (!Array.isArray(functions)) return [];`). **Right** — an object key cannot repeat; triage's CONTROL, pinned.
5. **Byte-identical twins are refused; the lowered string-ref form with a repeated `name` is refused; suffixed refs (`kc_a`, `kc_a__2`) are accepted as two names.** **Right.** Two array entries are two registrations under one name whatever they hold (`collectBundleFunctionEntries` in `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:2290`ff writes `out[item.name] = fn` per item, last wins; the engine's `functions` is a `Map`). A build never emits a repeated name, so refusing a repeated lowered name loses nothing; `kc_a__2` is a distinct string.
6. **`strict: false` skips the check.** **Right** — the only call of `validateCrossReferences` is `defineStack`'s strict path, so the reach equals every sibling cross-reference check's; pinned as kept, not widened.
7. **No change to `objectstack build`, `lowerCallables`, the runtime or `composeStacks`.** **Right** — the file list is `packages/spec` only; the triage fences hold.
8. **Public surface unchanged.** **Right.** `collectDuplicateFunctionNameErrors` is a module-private `function`; the diff adds no `export`; `check:api-surface` read `unchanged` per the report and the schema shape is untouched, so no generated artifact moves (`check:generated` 14/14 current; CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` answers it finally).
9. **D3 semantic entry `18.stack-functions-array-duplicate-name-refused.ts`, no D2 conversion.** **Right.** `PROTOCOL_VERSION` on `main` is `18.0.0` with spec at `17.7.0` in pre mode (`next`) and the v18 line open, so step 18 is the current step (347 step-18 entries, none at 19). `registry.ts` is gitignored and regenerated from `registry.ts.template` + `entries/` on every build, so no committed artifact is missing; `check:upgrade-guide --check` and `check:spec-changes` compare no committed copy. The entry carries every required field (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`), no `conversionIds`, and its `id` is the one the changeset's `adr-0087: registered` marker names — new in this diff, as the gate's `registered` rule requires. "Not convertible: which entry keeps the name is the author's" is the correct D3-only disposition.
10. **Pins** (`stack-duplicate-function-name.test.ts`, 10 cases): envelope + named subjects (name and exactly the indices), 3+2 collisions as 2 findings, the twins, the object-less stack, the lowered form, one aggregate with a duplicate action key, `strict: false`, and the three CONTROLs. **Right**; the refusal cases differ from a CONTROL by one name, and the source ablation went 6 red / 4 green in the predicted direction.

The factual sentences the docblock, changeset and D3 entry carry were checked on `origin/main`: cross-stack refusal (`composeFunctions`), last-wins source boot (`collectBundleFunctionEntries`), the lookup-by-name namespace (the `functions` schema's own docblock). The exit codes per door (validate 1, build 2, serve 1) and the before/after tables are the dev's CLI readings, consistent with `loadConfig` running the author's strict `defineStack`; not re-run here.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset** `.changeset/22902-stack-functions-array-duplicate-name-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`; summary `feat(spec)!:`; `**BREAKING**` banner; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; `adr-0087: registered stack-functions-array-duplicate-name-refused`; FROM → TO table and the one-line fix. **Matches what the diff publishes:** an accept-set narrowing of the published `defineStack` door in a released package — a changeset is owed (⛔ not `skip-changeset`), and this one carries all four breaking-ness signals the ADR-0087 gate reads (banner, `!`, the `narrowing` arm, the registered D3 id).
- **Grade `minor` on a breaking narrowing: right.** ADR-0087 § "Ratified: the pre-launch launch-window exemption", level-half amendment (#18003): "Pre-GA, a metadata-facing retirement or break ships `minor`, carrying the BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition entry"; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces the same convention and states its GA end condition, which has not occurred (spec `17.7.0`, pre mode `next`). Triage's "a major's change: v18 … otherwise v19" reads as the PROTOCOL-major axis, which that amendment names as a separate axis from the npm level; the D3 entry at step 18 answers it. In the lockstep `fixed` group with `major` changesets already pending (e.g. `22080-v18-line-opens.md`), `minor` moves no version number, as the report says.
- **`Clause-②:` line.** PR body and changeset both read `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — the legal spelling for a narrowing (`execution-duties.md`: a card narrowing a published accept-set is `no`; AGENTS.md: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, only `no (widening)` is malformed). Triage's `yes (narrowing)` was off-rule; the claim corrected it and the two carriers agree. The arm carries the level axis, so `check-changeset-no-major` reads `minor` as the owed grade (`Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head).

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none. Dev flags (7 deviations, 2 out-of-scope findings, 4 acceptance notes), each answered:

- **D3 entry added though the claim allowed it only on demand** — answered: the gate refuses `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` on a body carrying a prescription (its rule, read in the script header); the dev measured it on a committed probe after noting a working-tree probe is a no-op. The claim's condition was met exactly. Accepted.
- **Grade `minor`** — judged right in ② above.
- **`main` merged before the gate union (3 commits, no `packages/spec` change)** — the net diff against `main` is the 4 files; package tests ran on an identical spec tree. Accepted.
- **Examples' "before" baseline taken on the dist-ablated build, not a separate base build** — a valid control for "the collector does not change the examples' answers"; the duplicate fixture's before row is a real base build. Accepted.
- **Census measured only at the contract door; downstream per sibling key NOT measured** — triage asked for the list of array-of-named members lacking a same-stack refusal, which the PR body gives (20 keys at `os validate`, 6 more at `defineStack`, 4 already refused, the non-named keys excluded with reasons). Downstream loss per key is honestly marked unmeasured. **Escalated to the seat as the one batch card** triage fenced ("⛔ not one card per key"); the ACCEPT already owns filing it. Not a defect of this PR.
- **Attribution footer** — the PR body ends with the session-URL footer AGENTS.md prescribes. Commit trailers are outside this review's input set (body, file list, net diff); the pre-push check and CI are their gate.
- **Shallow fetch of `621a487607` into the shared `.git`** — a process note with no contract effect; noted.
- **Out-of-scope 2 / acceptance note 1: `strict: false` skips the refusal; `os validate` and `os build` then read the lowered, already-suffixed names** — the boundary every cross-reference check shares; pinned as kept. Noted, no carrier, as filed.
- **Acceptance notes 2 and 4 (PM assumption 4 re-measured on current `main`; the three doors' exits)** — consistent with `loadConfig` running the author's strict `defineStack`; the dev's readings, accepted.
- **Reviewer note, not a dev flag:** the D3 entry omits `relevantWhen`. The surface lives only under the top-level `functions` key and `'functions'` is a legal `SemanticRelevanceKey`, so `{ kind: 'stack-declares', keys: ['functions'] }` would let `os migrate meta` count the TODO as absent for a stack with no `functions` at all. Omission is the contract's default ("the entry is then always listed"; 20 of 347 step-18 entries carry a question) and keeps D3's never-silence posture, so this is a follow-on improvement, not a finding. Adding it is a reviewed edit enumerated by `semantic-relevance.test.ts`.
- **Not measured locally, CI's:** `check:dts-closure` (no `.d.ts` on 58 locally `OS_SKIP_DTS=1` packages; spec not on its list) and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (prerequisite not met). The `Build Core` and `Lint & Repo Gates` runs on this head answer both.

**Check-runs on `70c36c11516537a824ada5dadc0bf8c6455f43d3`, as read at 2026-10-12T03:46Z** — 36 runs: 13 `success` (Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · source gates, filter); 6 `skipped` (Auto Label and Check PR Size re-runs, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke ×2); **17 `in_progress`, which are not passes** (Build Core, Check Changeset re-run, Dogfood Regression Gate 1–3/3, Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint & Repo Gates, Temporal Conformance, Test Core 1–6/6, Type Check · consumer gates, · debt ledger, · workspace). This verdict is on the diff's contract; the seat separately requires every check green before the queue.
